name: Dermachrome — The Concealment Aesthetic
creator: Attributed to stylist collective Pale Margin, Tier 3 Chicago Hub
description: A fashion movement built around matching prosthetic covers, synthetic skin panels, and chromatic subdermal pigment injections to one's natural skin tone with near-perfect accuracy, rendering all augmentation invisible to the naked eye. Practitioners consider the hidden chrome a private matter — a philosophy of interiority over display. The movement carries a quiet defiance: in a world that monetizes visible augmentation, invisibility becomes a form of sovereignty.
cultural_impact: Dermachrome forced corponation augmentation manufacturers to develop the lucrative 'Skintrue' product line, inadvertently funding the movement that resisted their branding logic. It also became a privacy-rights symbol in the years surrounding the Chrome Mandate debates.
controversy: Critics from chrome maximalist communities accused Dermachrome practitioners of shame-passing and internalized augment stigma. Corponation Axiom briefly attempted to ban certain concealment-grade synthetic skin panels as 'identity obfuscation materials' in 2199.
story_hooks: A Dermachrome practitioner is the only witness to a Spire-level crime — investigators must find them without knowing what their body actually looks like.
A young Tier 2 worker saves for years to afford Skintrue panels, only to discover the concealment carries a corporate tracking signature embedded in the pigment.
A Dermachrome collective is accused of harboring unregistered military-grade augments beneath their covers — the truth is far more complicated.
